availability_check._doc: Per-host bucket caps for the RDAP availability stage, derived from a runtime budget. For each distinct RDAP host bucket, cap = floor(max_runtime_per_host_seconds * workers / effective_throttle), where effective_throttle comes from api_min_interval_seconds.rdap_per_host[host] -> rdap -> 2.0, and workers from rdap_concurrency.per_host[host] -> default_workers_per_host -> 1. Buckets exceeding their cap are random-shuffled (seed = today's date int) then truncated. global_cap is a safety net against pathological days where filter behaviour leaks far more survivors than expected; today's typical 14k lexical survivors fits below it. Replaced the prior length-asc trim (max_candidates_for_enrichment=1000) on 2026-05-04 — that heuristic biased toward already-registered short names without improving Wayback-signal density. max_runtime_per_host_seconds bumped 900 -> 2700 on 2026-05-05 to compensate for slower throttles after the ban events; per-host candidate volume stays similar (each bucket still wall-clock-bounded, now at 45 min not 15 min). Total RDAP phase wall-clock = max(bucket_runtimes) since all buckets run concurrently, so the slowest bucket caps total at ~45 min. NOTE: max_runtime_per_host_seconds is intentionally kept aligned with the top-level availability_budget_seconds (2700 s as of 2026-05-07). availability_budget_seconds is the global wall-clock deadline applied across the entire RDAP phase inside validate_availability(); when it's smaller than max_runtime_per_host_seconds, it pre-empts per-host completion and behaves as a guillotine (the bug 2026-05-07 surfaced — 1500 s was firing before any bucket finished its planned 2700 s). With both at 2700 s the global deadline acts as a redundant safety net rather than the binding constraint.

api_request_timeout_seconds._doc: Per-enricher request timeout. Falls back to request_timeout_seconds when unset. Wayback CDX and crt.sh frequently take 15-30s under peak load — their 10s default forced ~80% of calls to time out on 2026-04-30. The retry-on-timeout logic in wayback.py / crtsh.py adds a second safety net.

rdap_concurrency._doc: Per-host concurrency for the RDAP availability check. The pipeline buckets candidates by RDAP host and runs each bucket in its own ThreadPoolExecutor; all buckets execute simultaneously. Within a bucket, workers serialize on the existing thread-safe HostThrottle so per-host request rate never exceeds api_min_interval_seconds.rdap (or rdap_per_host) — concurrency only ever fans out *across* hosts. Defaults are safe (1 worker per host); per_host stays empty until empirically validated against a specific registry. Lookup: per_host[host] → default_workers_per_host → 1.

api_min_interval_seconds._doc: Minimum interval between requests to each API host. With max_concurrent_enrichments=1 (sequential) and multiplicative 0.75-1.25× jitter applied per call, actual rates are ~25% slower than the nominal value. Tightened 2026-04-30 after 503/502 storms with the previous 1.0s/0.4s/0.2s settings. RDAP global default raised 0.4 → 2.0 on 2026-05-05 after multiple registries banned us (identitydigital 24h, PIR 1h) under the previous default — a new/unknown registry must default to a safe rate.

rdap_per_host._doc: Per-host overrides for RDAP. Falls through to api_min_interval_seconds.rdap when host not listed. Recalibrated 2026-05-05 after the first uncapped run produced multiple Retry-After bans: identitydigital.services 24-hour (1069 checked, 949 unknown), publicinterestregistry.org 1-hour (1966 checked, 1628 unknown), GMO 49 unknowns at 3.0s. Conservative empirical settings with safety margin — accept reduced volume in exchange for zero ban risk going forward, because a permanent ban from any registry would block the pipeline for that TLD entirely. Sources per host: identitydigital banned today → 5.0s (most cautious); PIR banned today → 3.0s (matches GMO caution); GMO 49 unknowns at 3.0s → 4.0s defensive bump; Google + nic.biz degraded but not banned → 2.0s; centralnic + radix clean at 0.4s but only 2250 candidates each so 1.0s defensive margin.
